cbhNotes.title: What the Absolute Universe is
cbhNotes.body: Spilled out of October 2024’s DC All In Special #1. A new DCU defined by Darkseid energy, with new status quos for the Trinity and later the wider pantheon. Closest DC analogue to Marvel’s Ultimate line, plus Elseworlds-style premises (Batman isn’t rich; Wonder Woman was raised in Hell). Early going is defined as much by the art — Dragotta, Sherman, and the rest — as by the premises.

cbhNotes.title: The two meanings of “Absolute”
cbhNotes.body: DC also uses Absolute for oversized reprint hardcovers (Absolute Watchmen, Absolute Batman: Haunted Knight, etc.). If it didn’t start in 2024 or later and it is not on this list, it is not the new Absolute Universe.

cbhNotes.title: Do the launch books intersect?
cbhNotes.body: After the first three issues of each, Comic Book Herald says you can read each series on its own. The list is publication order so you can mirror the original experience, but you do not need every title to keep up.

cbhNotes.title: All In Special
cbhNotes.body: The only comic that even pretends to be required before Absolute Batman, and CBH still calls it optional — more confusing than useful for brand-new readers. It does establish that Darkseid created this universe, which will matter later.

cbhNotes.title: Prime DCU
cbhNotes.body: You need zero prime-DCU reading. Snyder’s New 52 Court of Owls is a fun comparison piece, not homework.

cbhNotes.title: Absolute Evil
cbhNotes.body: Essential one-shot interlude for the back half of 2025 and 2026. Focus on Joker, Ra’s al Ghul, Dr. Thawne, Veronica Cale, Hector Hammond.

cbhNotes.title: The Batman / Wonder Woman crossover
cbhNotes.body: First official crossover: two issues, Wonder Woman #15 then Batman #16.

cbhNotes.title: DC K.O.
cbhNotes.body: Continuation of All In on the prime-DCU side. CBH says you can skip all of it if you only care about Absolute.
